subject: health
title: Sleep and Screens
about: Why sleep matters (growing, remembering, feeling good), who needs more of it, a bedtime routine, screens off and out of the bedroom at night, eye breaks, and choosing play time over screen time. Sleep and screens are a bridge topic: NC puts them under 1.PCH.1 (behaviors that promote health) and 1.NPA.2.2 (fun activities in and out of school), plus PE.1.HF.3.3 (join in actively).
tip: Draw his bedtime routine as four pictures on a card by his bed and let him check them off.

cards.q: What does your body do while you sleep?
cards.note: Your body does a lot of its growing while you sleep.

cards.q: Sleep helps your brain do what with the things you learned today?
cards.note: While you sleep, your brain files away what you learned.

cards.q: You did not get enough sleep. How might you feel?
cards.note: Not enough sleep makes it hard to listen, learn and be kind.

cards.q: Who needs more sleep each night, a first grader or a grown-up?
cards.note: Kids 6 to 12 need 9 to 12 hours. Most grown-ups need 7 or more.

cards.q: What do you call the same steps you do every night before bed?
cards.note: Bath, teeth, pajamas, story, lights out. Same order every night.

cards.q: Which one belongs in a good bedtime routine?
cards.note: Calm, quiet things tell your body it is almost time to sleep.

cards.q: What should be turned off before bedtime?
cards.note: Turn screens off at least an hour before bed.

cards.q: Does screen light before bed make it easier or harder to fall asleep?
cards.note: Bright screen light tells your brain it is still daytime.

cards.q: Where should a tablet or phone sleep at night?
cards.note: Screens charge in the kitchen or living room. Bedrooms are for sleeping.

cards.q: What kind of room helps you fall asleep?
cards.note: A night light is fine if it is dim.

cards.q: Which is a calm thing to do right before sleep?
cards.note: A story with a grown-up is a perfect last step.

cards.q: You look at a screen for a long time. What do your eyes need?
cards.note: Blink, look out a window, and rest your eyes.

cards.q: After 20 minutes on a screen, look far away for how long?
cards.note: The 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.

cards.q: Which one makes your muscles stronger?
cards.note: Screens are fun, but your body grows strong by moving.

cards.q: Who decides how long you may use a screen?
cards.note: Screen rules keep time for play, sleep and family.

cards.q: Your screen time is over. What do you do?
cards.a: turn it off and go play
cards.note: Turning it off the first time you are asked shows you are growing up.

cards.q: Why do you have a bedtime?
cards.note: A set bedtime helps you fall asleep faster and wake up ready.

cards.q: It is time to move in PE class. What do you do?
cards.sayQ: It is time to move in gym class. What do you do?
cards.a: join in and try your best
cards.note: Joining in is how you get stronger and have more fun.
